findings.problem: SampleWorkflow is a flat struct with no typestate enum or transition discipline; all fields are independently mutable and there is no compile-time guarantee that only valid lifecycle combinations exist
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct SampleWorkflow with status="sent" but is_sent=false, or is_validated=true and status="draft", producing logically inconsistent state that the type system cannot reject
findings.fix: Replace the struct fields with a `WorkflowStatus` enum that owns the lifecycle (e.g., `Draft`, `Validated { id: WorkflowId }`, `Sent { id: WorkflowId, sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`) and remove all lifecycle booleans and the status String from the data type

findings.problem: `status: String` allows any string value including invalid lifecycle states; callers can set status to any string without domain validation
findings.failure_mode: a caller passes `status: "xyz"` and the system treats it as a valid state, or string comparison is used for state checks which is fragile and error-prone
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with a `WorkflowStatus` enum variant; remove the String field entirely so only valid states are representable

findings.problem: `is_validated: bool` and `is_sent: bool` are independent lifecycle booleans that can contradict each other and the status string; the type system cannot enforce a valid transition order
findings.failure_mode: caller sets is_validated=true and is_sent=true without ever calling mark_sent, or sets is_sent=true without setting status="sent", creating inconsistent state with no compile-time guard
findings.fix: Encode the lifecycle as enum variants with explicit transitions; remove both bool fields so the enum variant itself proves which milestones have been reached

findings.problem: `sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>` allows the sent timestamp to be None while other fields suggest the workflow is sent; Option splits lifecycle data from the lifecycle state itself
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent sets is_sent=true but does not populate sent_at_epoch_ms, leaving the struct in a state where is_sent=true but sent_at_epoch_ms=None — a logically inconsistent combination that is valid at the type level
findings.fix: Move `sent_at_epoch_ms: u64` into the `Sent` enum variant so the timestamp is only present when the workflow is genuinely in the Sent state; the type system guarantees consistency

findings.problem: `id: String` is a raw primitive that carries no domain constraints; any string is accepted as a valid workflow ID with no format, length, or uniqueness rules enforced at the type level
findings.failure_mode: empty strings, malformed IDs, or duplicate IDs can flow into core logic; string equality on IDs is ambiguous vs. struct equality on domain values
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct WorkflowId(String)` (or `NonEmptyString` wrapped) with a smart constructor that validates the ID format, and use it everywhere the workflow ID is referenced

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts SampleWorkflow with raw String fields and mutable inner fields directly; raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly and mark_sent silently accepts any pre-existing state as valid input
findings.failure_mode: a caller passes a SampleWorkflow where status="draft" but is_sent=true, and mark_sent does not validate the transition — it just overwrites status and sets the flag, treating any input as valid rather than enforcing a state-transition invariant
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a fallible transition function that takes the current state enum and returns a new state enum with Err for invalid transitions; move string construction into a parse function that returns Result<SampleWorkflow, TransitionError>

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for mark_sent or any hot path; performance claims cannot be verified and allocation patterns are unmeasured
findings.failure_mode: unmeasured code may have hidden allocation costs (e.g., `.to_string()` on line 10 allocates a new String each call) that compound under load; no baseline exists to detect regressions
findings.fix: Add a benchmark for mark_sent that measures allocation count (via allocator instrumentation or `mimalloc` stats), string allocation on the status field, and overall latency; report allocations per call

findings.problem: `.to_string()` on line 10 always allocates a new String for the status field even when the status is already "sent"; this is an unbounded allocation on every call
findings.failure_mode: under high throughput, repeated mark_sent calls allocate a new heap String each time, increasing GC pressure and tail latency with no benefit over reusing a static or interned representation
findings.fix: Replace with an enum variant that has no heap-allocated string data for status; use `Cow<'static, str>` or the enum itself to avoid allocation entirely

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any function
no profiler evidence for allocation patterns
no allocation budget or try_reserve usage anywhere
no command-truth evidence (no build/test commands run)
no second-ring evidence for any performance or safety claim
residual_risk: Review is static source analysis only. No commands were executed. The code has no compilation or test evidence. All findings are based on type-level and structural analysis against the Holzman Rust candidate skill. The fundamental architecture (flat struct with raw primitives instead of a typestate enum) is a BLOCKER that cannot be waived. A full repair requires replacing the entire SampleWorkflow definition with a domain-driven typestate enum, adding a WorkflowId newtype, removing lifecycle booleans, and implementing fallible state transitions.
